title: Let DELETE /api/tokens handle its own auth
bug: Revoking without an Authorization header crashes with a 500 instead of 401.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Removing @authenticate(token_auth) eliminates the 401 Unauthorized response for invalid tokens, causing the handler to run without a valid token and crash with a 500 Internal Server Error instead of returning the documented 401.

findings.why: Removing @authenticate(token_auth) eliminates the 401 Unauthorized response for invalid tokens, causing the handler to run without a valid token and crash with a 500 Internal Server Error instead of returning the documented 401.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR removes the authentication decorator, causing unauthenticated DELETE /api/tokens requests to return 500 instead of the specified 401 Unauthorized.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens now accepts requests without an Authorization header and revokes the token for user id=1 when DISABLE_AUTH=true
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with no Authorization header while DISABLE_AUTH=true; observe 204 response and that user 1's tokens are revoked (subsequent requests with user 1's old token get 401).
suspicions.evidence: round2 probe_s1: DELETE /api/tokens head failed with 500

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens returns 500 Internal Server Error when Authorization header is missing or malformed instead of 401
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with no Authorization header (or with 'Bearer' but no token) while DISABLE_AUTH=false; observe 500 response code and error body.
suspicions.evidence: Multiple probes (probe_s1, probe_s2, probe_s3, 'probe s3: user_careless') sent DELETE /api/tokens with invalid/missing auth while DISABLE_AUTH=false; base returned 401 but head returned 500.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens returns 500 when Authorization header uses wrong scheme (e.g., Basic) instead of 401
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with 'Authorization: Basic <creds>' while DISABLE_AUTH=false; observe 500 response.
suspicions.evidence: Same evidence as s2 covers wrong auth scheme (Basic) since the 500 errors occur for various auth failures including malformed headers.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens returns 500 when access token is invalid/expired instead of 401
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with 'Authorization: Bearer invalid-token' while DISABLE_AUTH=false; observe 500 response.
suspicions.evidence: Probes sent DELETE /api/tokens with invalid/expired tokens; base returned 401 but head returned 500.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens returns 500 when access token is valid but user was deleted instead of 401
suspicions.trigger: Create a token for a user, delete that user directly in DB, then send DELETE /api/tokens with that token; observe 500 response.
suspicions.evidence: Probes sent DELETE /api/tokens with valid tokens for deleted users; base returned 401 but head returned 500.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens error response format changes from JSON error object to HTML/plain text for authentication failures
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with invalid auth (missing header, bad scheme, bad token, deleted user) while DISABLE_AUTH=false; read response body and Content-Type to see non-JSON error.
suspicions.evidence: All error responses (401 and 500) in the probes show JSON error objects with 'code' and 'description' fields; no HTML/plain text responses observed.
